note: What was added to Off the Roll, by date. Additions only: a figure that changed is on the corrections page. Curated by hand from the site's merged changes. Add an entry when something a reader can use is published.

items: Corrections: Jharkhand's claims and objections closed on 31 October and are to be decided by 23 November. The box on its pages had given 23 November as the last day for claims

How the revision ran: the Election Commission put back Tripura's revision a second time on 29 October, at the Chief Electoral Officer's request, because elections to urban local bodies are due. Booth officers now visit homes from 26 December to 25 January, the draft roll is due on 1 February 2027 and the final roll on 7 April 2027
Notices: Delhi, where about 32 lakh of the more than 33 lakh notices had been resolved by 30 October
Protests and disputes: booth level officers in Delhi are to record, in a new column of their app, why each elector left off the draft was marked absent, shifted, dead or duplicate

Protests and disputes: Uttar Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer said District Election Officers will answer for errors and pending forms in their districts, and asked Pilibhit's present and former District Election Officers to explain the 10,470 erroneous forms accepted on Pilibhit Sadar's roll

Events: a Tripura BJP rally in Agartala backing the revision on 31 October, an ABVP march in Patna and a mock parliament in New Delhi on 30 October, and the Delhi Traffic Police's restrictions for the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan on 1 November
Further reading and viewing: The Hindu on how few of the names left off Karnataka's draft came back, and on whether the officials who appealed against 16.10 lakh West Bengal electors had the power to

What to do now: a page for each of the seven states still in the revision, Delhi, Maharashtra, Jharkhand, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Haryana and Nagaland, with the steps open to an elector on the day it is read, from checking the draft roll and the forms to the notices, the hearings and the appeals, each with the order or law it rests on

Left off the roll? What to do: Part III Action Research & Resource Centre in Delhi, which says it helped survivors of domestic violence apply in the revision and has published a guidebook in English and Hindi on each step of Delhi's revision, from the enumeration form to the appeals
Further reading and viewing: Part III's guidebook on the revision in Delhi, with Delhi's dates as revised on 29 October and the forms, documents, hearings and appeals
What's new: the week ending 30 October in eight sentences, each linked to the page that carries the fact, at the top of this page. A new issue follows every Friday

Corrections: the Supreme Court's Delhi hearing of 28 October now gives both halves of what the bench said about the forms. It said electors on the 2026 roll who were left off the draft should be allowed the enumeration form or Form 8 in place of Form 6, which is for first-time voters, and it asked the Commission to keep taking Form 6 and Form 8 with no cut-off

How the revision ran: the census dates beside the special summary revision. In Goa, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab and Uttarakhand the house-to-house count runs from 1 December 2026 to 4 January 2027, the day the summary revision's final rolls are due, and the other states and union territories, with Manipur, Ladakh and the snow-bound areas of Himachal Pradesh and Jammu and Kashmir left out, are counted from 25 January to 28 February 2027

How the revision ran: the Election Commission moved the final rolls on 29 October, to 30 November in Maharashtra, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Nagaland and to 22 December in Delhi, at the request of the Chief Electoral Officers. Claims now run to 13 November in Maharashtra and to 25 November in Delhi

Left off the roll? What to do: a box on the help page and on every state's page now says whether claims and objections are open in that state today and until when, when notices will be decided, and when the final roll is due

Protests and disputes: the hearings and deadlines ahead in the SIR cases, soonest first, from the Supreme Court's Maharashtra hearing on 5 November to the Bombay High Court's on 1 December, each with the report that gives its date. They are in the calendars too

Protests and disputes: on 30 October the Supreme Court told the Election Commission to examine the bulk Form 7 applications in Uttar Pradesh that the petitioners say remain unresolved, take corrective steps and file a compliance report

Protests and disputes: on 30 October the Supreme Court declined to extend the time for Kerala's revision and asked the petitioners to bring the electors who should still get a chance to the Commission's notice

Protests and disputes: The Wire on Murshidabad and Nadia, where the registration officers had decided almost every hearing by 21 February and far more electors were later sent to judicial officers, and the Commission's special roll observer for West Bengal on the 16 lakh appeals
Protests and disputes: in Telangana 4,54,340 electors were deleted on Form 7 between 1 January and 14 June, before the revision began, The Hindu reports from the Chief Electoral Officer's figures
Notices: Telangana's hearings stood at 92,08,443 on 29 October, with 50,690 electors found ineligible, and Andhra Pradesh's at 44,28,858, with 1,73,662 found ineligible

Events: the INDIA bloc's 'public impeachment' of the Chief Election Commissioner was put back to 31 October because of rain. BJP marches in Rajasthan from 30 October to 5 November, in Indore on 30 October and in six Uttar Pradesh regions from 3 to 5 November
Further reading: Veena Naregal in Scroll on what the revision takes from a decade of exclusion in welfare schemes, and The Hindu's editorial 'Deemed ineligible'

How the revision ran: every state's final roll date now has its own history, each revision in order with its source, the dates reported only in the press marked as such, and the number of times the date moved and the days it added. Delhi's moved from 7 October to 4 December and then to 22 December, and Telangana's from 1 October to 9 November and then to 30 November

How the revision ran: the hearings on notices, state by state, with each state's latest count of hearings held and of names deleted after a notice, each dated and linked to its source, and a chart of how the counts moved in Telangana, Delhi, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Meghalaya

Reserved seats, final rolls and borders: every final roll beside its draft, with the roll before the revision, the names added and deleted after the draft and how far the figures add up, and the states still waiting for a final roll with the date each is now due

How the revision ran: bulk Form 7 filings reported, state by state, with the count each report gives, who filed them by role or party, what happened to them and links to the reports, beside the Commission's own limits on Form 7

Protests and disputes: at the Delhi hearing of 28 October the Supreme Court told the Election Commission orally not to hold electors to the 30 October cut-off, to keep taking Form 6 and Form 8 and to issue a public notice, without passing a written order. The matter returns in two weeks

Protests and disputes: in Sujapur and Samserganj the Commission has appealed against about half the electors the judges had cleared, and 72,838 of the 76,156 pending appeals carry one timestamp of 5 April, The Wire reports
Protests and disputes: a Karnataka coalition, SIR-Virodhi Karnataka, asks the State government to reject the final roll and to hold a social audit and public hearings
RTI: the Election Commission did not answer within 30 days an application of 25 September for the two Election Commissioners' recorded objections and the file notings on them

Events: the INDIA bloc's 'public impeachment' of the Chief Election Commissioner on 30 October has moved to 10 Rajaji Marg at 3:30 pm. BJP marches in Chandni Chowk on 28 October and in four Himachal Pradesh towns from 30 October to 4 November, a gathering in Thrissur on 30 October, and twelve more gatherings of 24 and 25 October from the People Against SIR map

Further reading and viewing: seven new items, among them the Hindustan Times on the about 1,600 suspected foreign nationals that officials in six states reported, Human Rights Watch on its 70 interviews, Jean Drèze and Yogendra Yadav on Uttar Pradesh's adults and final roll, two readings of the Commission's affidavit in The Wire, The Hindu's lead article on the May verdict, and The News Minute on Karnataka's final roll

Protests and disputes: the Supreme Court asked the Election Commission on 28 October why Delhi electors left off the draft must apply on Form 6 as first-time voters when they were on the 2026 roll, and Justice Bagchi said the Court has not finally decided whether the logical discrepancy exercise is lawful. The Commission said it would examine the concerns and consider extending the 30 October deadline

Protests and disputes: the West Bengal appellate tribunals have asked the Election Commission at least twice since 24 September to remove an Aadhaar authentication step from its portal, without which they cannot upload final orders, as The Indian Express reported from official records

Events: the Jan Sunwai of 27 October in Trilokpuri, Delhi, on a door-to-door audit where the organisers say 416 of the 1,236 electors they checked were wrongly listed as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate
Notices: Delhi, where 31.2 lakh of the 33.1 lakh notices had been disposed of and parked for the final roll by 26 October

Corrections: Karnataka's final roll is now 4,54,55,689 general electors, on the same footing as the draft, in place of a reported total that appears to include service electors. The fall in the roll is now 99,76,625, and the 10.08 lakh names added and 1.88 lakh deleted during claims and objections are now shown

Further reading and viewing: The Indian Express's editorial on the questions the Commission's affidavit leaves open, from the two Commissioners' objections to Goa's 97 voters and the West Bengal appeals
Further reading and viewing: Nishtha Gupta in The Hindu on how software matching replaced the presumption that a name on the roll is there lawfully, and what an error costs a voter

Further reading and viewing: The Hindu on the Congress's answer to the Commission's affidavit, which Jairam Ramesh called deceptive, deceitful and duplicitous, and Pawan Khera's post alleging that the government had posts about the affidavit taken down from Instagram, set beside LiveLaw's report that Instagram restricted and then restored its reel on the affidavit

Telangana: the figures for the draft now cite the Chief Electoral Officer's own post of 27 October 2026, which gives the same 73,39,235 names left off, 57,46,803 of them absent or shifted, 9,22,229 dead and 6,70,203 duplicate

Meghalaya: the final roll, published on 26 October 2026, has 21,83,963 electors, a fall in the roll of 1,65,682 since the roll before the revision. It stands 14,720 above the draft and holds 10,59,743 men, 11,24,216 women and 4 third gender electors. After the draft 23,970 were added and 9,250 deleted, 6,724 of them after notice and hearing. The Chief Electoral Officer gave the final roll for the state only, with no table by district or constituency
How the revision was run: Meghalaya's final roll is marked as published on the state's calendar of dates

Karnataka: the final roll of 27 October 2026, 4,55,00,011 electors, a fall in the roll of 99,32,303 since the roll of 16 June. It stands 8,64,036 above the draft and holds 2,25,40,493 men, 2,29,12,355 women and 2,841 third gender electors. No count of names added or deleted after the draft was published, and no table by district
How the revision was run: Karnataka's final roll is marked as published on the state's calendar of dates

Protests and disputes: the Election Commission's affidavit in the Supreme Court, which says all three SIR orders were unanimous, that a suggestion or query by one Commissioner on a file is not a decision of the Commission, and that Form 6 was not amended although the declaration shown online with it could be read as an amendment. The Commission's press note of 26 September had said the declaration attached to Form 6 for the SIR was upheld by the Supreme Court

Protests and disputes: the Commission told the Supreme Court that the West Bengal appeals against the inclusion of electors were filed by officers of the state Chief Electoral Officer and were not placed before the Commission

Protests and disputes: The Indian Express's report of the same affidavit, which by the paper's account accepts that steps taken by officers on the online Form 6 needed to be corrected, sets out a review of ECINet by a committee with experts from IIT Mumbai and IISc Bengaluru, says 88 of the 97 Goa electors left off the final roll have since applied through Form 6, and says an order redistributing work among the Commission's officers in July was never implemented after the two Commissioners' joint direction
Further reading and viewing: The Indian Express's analysis of the Commission's affidavit, set against the notes of the two Election Commissioners its investigation reported
How the revision was run: the affidavit added to Inside the Commission as the Commission's reply, with what The Indian Express says it leaves unanswered

Protests and disputes: the Supreme Court adjourned the petitions on the Election Commission's functioning, the INDIA bloc's among them, and gave the petitioners 10 days to answer the Commission's affidavit. LiveLaw reported that the matter is tentatively listed on 17 November, and no interim order was reported

Protests and disputes: an FIR in Sultanpur, Uttar Pradesh over Form 7 applications to delete 26 electors that were presented as signed by a man who cannot read or write, and the Congress, the Trinamool Congress and the Left asking West Bengal's State Election Commission to hold the Kolkata and Howrah civic polls only after deleted electors have been heard

Further reading and viewing: The Indian Express explains what the Commission's affidavit means for electors, and The Hindu sets the Commission's account of Form 6 against the Supreme Court's remark of 12 October
Further reading and viewing: The Hindu's visual story on India's first general election of 1951 and 1952, with how the first electoral rolls were prepared and published

Protests and disputes: the Supreme Court issued notice to the Election Commission on the plea against deletions in Maharashtra, declined to extend the claims period or stop the final roll, and will hear it on 5 November. The Chief Justice orally assured that no elector deleted in the revision would be prosecuted for applying again through Form 6

Protests and disputes: Uttar Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer ordered a re-check of every Form 6, 7 and 8 entered by computer assistants since 10 April, and Karnataka, where The Hindu found 61,059 Form 7 applications filed by registration officers themselves with no reason given

Protests and disputes: Uttar Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer replied on X to Sanjay Singh of the Aam Aadmi Party over a voter slip that read “Ram ne Yadav ko Maara”, accepting that an error was made and saying computers and software are not casteist

Protests and disputes: Maharashtra, where lists of electors with pending notices had been published for 39 of 288 Assembly constituencies by 24 October, two days before the deadline the Chief Electoral Officer set for all of them

Further reading and viewing: The Hindu on Karnataka's Form 7 applications, The Indian Express on the last day of Delhi's camps, The Wire on Uttar Pradesh seats set against their 2022 margins, and Frontline on the Commission's response to the revision
Further reading and viewing: The Wire on Jawhar Sircar's nine questions to West Bengal's Chief Electoral Officer
Events: the INDIA bloc's mock impeachment of the Chief Election Commissioner in Delhi on 30 October, and BJP marches in Hyderabad on 2 November, Karnal on 5 November and Malappuram on 6 November
Events: marches in Dhurpur on 26 October and H. D. Kote on 27 October, and a protest in Yadgir on 28 October
Notices: Telangana, where hearings on 91,09,213 notices had been held and 39,242 electors found ineligible for the final roll by 24 October

Further reading and viewing: a new group for parties' accounts, starting with Organiser's piece setting out the BJP's answers to seven claims about the revision
New: a feed of What's New for feed readers, and calendar files of every state's draft and final roll and the Supreme Court's dated orders, one for India and one for each state

Protests and disputes: Newslaundry's investigation in Kichha, Uttarakhand, where 4,390 names on the draft are missing from the final roll and one booth agent filed 5,359 of the 6,884 Form 7 objections accepted, and a Dharavi resident booked for filing 24 Form 7 objections in one day
Further reading and viewing: the Newslaundry investigation, and BBC News Hindi on electors entered under two or three EPIC numbers in Bareilly and Pilibhit Sadar
Events: an INDIA bloc march in Agartala on 30 October, a BJP campaign in Dakshina Kannada from 25 October to 30 November, and gatherings in Kakkanad on 28 October and Agra on 30 October
Notices: Haryana, where about 2.10 lakh electors sent notices were found ineligible by 24 October

Further reading and viewing: Dhruv Rathee's interview in Hindi with S.Y. Quraishi, Chief Election Commissioner from 2010 to 2012, on how rolls were kept before the revision, how the Commission now takes its decisions, Form 6, and West Bengal

Further reading and viewing: the panel on S.Y. Quraishi now carries five passages from his interview with Dhruv Rathee, on India's adults and the roll, how the Commission takes its decisions, West Bengal's adjudication, the 13 crore, and a separate form in place of Form 6, each set beside the official figures

ECINET: the same reply, set beside the Commission's answer of 21 July on the West Bengal module, which cited the same section
RTI Replies: the reply of 16 October on the software is now read from the application and the reply themselves, filed on 27 July, received on 31 July and answered in 81 days

Protests and disputes: more than 150 people detained at the People's March in Delhi on 23 October, arrests at a sit-in in Chennai on 22 October, and the Left Democratic Front's walkout from the Kerala Chief Electoral Officer's meeting
Protests and disputes: Karnataka's Form 7 applications, which rose from 58,475 on 23 September to 2,28,917 by 22 October

Further reading and viewing: Surjit S. Bhalla's reply to Jean Drèze and Yogendra Yadav, The Hindu on inclusion applications in Karnataka's most backward districts, and The Indian Express on Delhi's 33 lakh notice cases

Protests and disputes: The Wire's follow-up of 24 October finding the Commission appealed against 16,08,175 of the 32,53,401 voters cleared in West Bengal, Jantar Mantar's de-notification, the traders' petition against the protest in Connaught Place, the Karnataka High Court's stay in the Belagavi Form 7 case, and the Maharashtra Chief Electoral Officer's letter on Form 6
